newsitem.title: USA: CME HOGS SEEN STEADY, PORK BELLIES STEADY TO LOWER.
newsitem.headline: CME HOGS SEEN STEADY, PORK BELLIES STEADY TO LOWER.

text.p: CME lean hog futures were expected to open about steady while pork belly futures were called steady to 0.400 cent per lb lower, livestock analysts said.

A lack of fundamentals to push hog futures significantly in any direction was noted, with mostly steady indications on cash markets providing little direction. Packers are operating with a positive cutout but hog runs appear adequate to meet demand. The market will be watching interior hog movement Friday morning, they said.
Futures held chart support near 72.100 cents a lb, basis October on Friday, and this may also provide support, some sources noted.
Spot August pork belly futures were expected to remain under pressure on weak cash belly prices. Belly prices have set back much further than expected, analysts said.
Cash bellies sank $12 per cwt last week after 14-16 lb supplies sold as high as $92 early in the week. Prices tumbled as low as $80 by Friday.
Next year contracts were seen showing little direction as they are mostly technical in nature at this time of year, analysts added.
